verses.text: From Paul, a servant of Jesus Christ. God called me to be an apostle and set me apart for his good news.
God promised this good news long ago through his prophets in the holy Scriptures.
It is about his Son. As a man, he was born from the family of David.
But by the Holy Spirit, and by rising from the dead, he was shown with power to be the Son of God. He is Jesus Christ our Lord.
Through him we received grace and the work of an apostle. Our work is to call people from all nations to trust and obey him, for the honour of his name.
You too are among those who are called to belong to Jesus Christ.
I write to all of you in Rome who are loved by God and called to be his holy people. Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for all of you, because people everywhere are talking about your faith.
God is my witness. I serve him with my whole heart as I tell the good news about his Son. I never stop remembering you in my prayers.
In my prayers I ask that now at last, by God's will, I may be able to come to you.
I long to see you, so that I can share some spiritual gift with you to make you strong.
I mean that you and I may encourage each other. Your faith will help me, and my faith will help you.
I want you to know, brothers and sisters, that I have often planned to come to you, but I have been stopped until now. I want to see some fruit among you, as I have among the other nations.
I owe a debt both to Greeks and to people who are not Greeks, both to the wise and to the unwise.
That is why I am so eager to tell the good news also to you who are in Rome.
I am not ashamed of the good news. It is the power of God that saves everyone who believes, first the Jew, and also the Greek.
In the good news, God shows how he makes people right with himself. It is by faith from start to finish. As the Scriptures say, "The person who is right with God will live by faith."
God's anger is being shown from heaven against all the godless and wrong things people do. They hold down the truth by the wrong things they do.
What can be known about God is plain to them, because God has made it plain.
Ever since the world was made, people have been able to see what God is like. His everlasting power and his nature as God are clear from the things he has made. So they have no excuse.
They knew God, but they did not honour him as God or give him thanks. Their thinking became empty, and their foolish hearts were darkened.
They claimed to be wise, but they became fools.
They traded the glory of the God who never dies for images that look like people who die, and like birds, animals and reptiles.
So God gave them over to the dirty desires of their hearts. They dishonoured their own bodies with one another.
They traded the truth about God for a lie. They worshipped and served what God created instead of the Creator himself, who is to be praised for ever. Amen.
Because of this, God gave them over to shameful desires. Their women traded natural sexual relations for unnatural ones.

In the same way, the men also left natural relations with women and burned with desire for one another. Men did shameful things with other men, and they received in themselves the due penalty for their wrong.
Since they did not think it worthwhile to keep God in their knowledge, God gave them over to a worthless mind, to do what should not be done.
They are full of every kind of wrong: sexual sin, evil, greed and hate. They are full of envy, murder, fighting, lies and spite. They gossip
and speak badly of others. They hate God. They are rude, proud and boastful. They invent ways of doing evil. They disobey their parents.
They are foolish, they break their promises, they have no love and no mercy.
They know God's just rule, that people who do such things deserve death. Yet they not only do them, but also approve of others who do them.
